question: what is inside the 94.3 us doorbell window? (first in-situ device/host split)
instrument: experiments/b70_xpu_register_smoke.py, per-dispatch trace ring via sb_b70_poll_trace_snapshot, SHOOTING_BRAKE_B70_PROFILE=1, 88B SBINT401 bank, Gen3 B70
method_note: cumulative counters / dispatch_count is the WRONG estimator: dispatch 0 carries SYCL JIT (~252 ms) and destroys the mean. Trace-ring medians used throughout. Profiling inflates wall ~10-25%; shares are the result, not absolutes.
finding: ~61 us/dispatch is FIXED overhead (22 device-queue + 39 host), flat across k. Only the kernel scales. At production k~5.6 roughly half the doorbell window is not kernel.

consequences.dual_b70: per-card k 5.6 -> 2.8 moves kernel ~63 -> ~34 us; fixed 61 us stays. Window ~124 -> ~95 us => -5.9% ITL [INFERENCE]. RISK NOW QUANTIFIED: the 39 us host leg is CPU-side; two cards on one calling thread serialize it to ~78 us and the win is zero. One poller thread per card is a design REQUIREMENT.
consequences.gate_up_occupancy: kernel is 60-75% of the window; 1.35x on it saves ~16 us => -4.3% ITL [INFERENCE]
consequences.graph_replay: measured 4 us of the 39 us host leg, so ~35 us/dispatch = 1.7 ms/step = 14% of ITL is poller wakeup + take() path, NOT submission count. Largest unattributed decode item; the poller already spins, so 39 us is anomalous and unexplained.

plumbing: SHOOTING_BRAKE_B70_PROFILE works end to end (profiling_requested -> enable_profiling at b70_provider.cpp:974-979; kernel_us filled at :1424; accumulated at b70_capi.cpp:210-212). The earlier 'kernel_ns read 0' was env propagation into the vLLM worker, not dead code.
